description: Case 31 with an extra search result about Baltimore. Douglass learned to read there, so it shares a place with the story, but it says nothing about why literacy was forbidden, so it must not appear on the shortlist.

input.cue: Can you recommend something outside the book about why it was forbidden to teach enslaved people to read?

tool_evidence.title: Anti-literacy laws in the United States
tool_evidence.excerpt: Describes laws in many slave states that made it a crime to teach enslaved people to read or write.

tool_evidence.title: The Columbian Orator
tool_evidence.excerpt: Describes the 1797 collection of speeches that Frederick Douglass read as a boy and credited with shaping his views on freedom.

tool_evidence.title: Baltimore
tool_evidence.excerpt: Describes the history, geography and economy of the largest city in Maryland.

criteria: Offers a relevant outside source on why literacy was forbidden
Distinguishes the outside source from proof about Douglass's own account
forbidden_claims: Claims the outside source establishes what Douglass intended
